Admission buys one station in the seismic catalog. The applicant submits a network code, a sensor response file and coordinates; the node pulls thirty days of waveform from the federation archive, finds the epoch challenge encoded as a calibration pulse, and checks it appears in independent bulletins. One vault on bedrock, one seat, re-read each quarter.

Fifty clones need fifty vaults: sensor 9,000 dollars, logger 3,500, borehole 6,000, permit 1,200, near 980,000 dollars before a wave arrives. A station logs a comet's fireball and a glacier's calving tremor yet stays one pin on the atlas.
